notes:
Summary: Mid-market SaaS vendor (product analytics + in-app insights). Completed 2-week Hosted API trial; now evaluating Dedicated for predictable latency and data isolation. Trial outcomes and next-phase asks below.

Top-level highlights:
- Trial run (2026-02-01 -> 2026-02-14): ran 120k total requests, ~18M tokens. Typical call pattern: short prompts (10-40 tokens) + medium completions (80-220 tokens). Token mix ~ 15% prompt / 85% completion by token count; by request ~ 1:1.
- Observed baseline QPS on Hosted: 6 QPS sustained; peak bursts to 32 QPS during internal demo times. 95th latency target from product: <= 200ms for short-turn conversational messages; they saw 95th ~ 180-250ms depending on model variant and length.
- Concurrency notes: concurrent sessions ~ 20 active users hitting API during peak demo; expected prod concurrency ~ 60-120 (concurrent user sessions producing parallel requests) when they roll to 2nd feature cohort.
- Cost sensitivity: cost per 1M tokens is a key metric for finance; they want predictable slot-based pricing (hence Dedicated).

Customer quotes / call snippets:
- "Hosted trial was fast to integrate, but we need predictable tail latency and isolation for PCI-adjacent workflows." — A. Patel (Head of Product)
- "If we can keep 95th <250ms and cut unit cost by ~30% vs hosted spikes, Dedicated is viable." — M. Lopez (Eng manager)

Detailed POC asks (Dedicated sizing + forecast):
- Baseline QPS target: 8 sustained QPS, headroom for 40 QPS bursts.
- Concurrency target: steady 80 concurrent requests, with peak concurrency 200 for 15-minute windows.
- Token forecast (monthly): 30M prompt tokens, 200M completion tokens -> ~230M tokens/mo. (approx 7.6B tokens/quarter).
- Model preference: open-model family + Redwood-verified medium-latency variant (quantized). Want fallback to cheaper quantized model for non-critical routes.
- Required SLOs: 99.9% availability, 95th latency <250ms for short-turn flows, ability to throttle/route to lower-cost variant automatically under contention.

POC milestones & timeline (CRM timeline style):
- 2026-01-22: Intro call (AE/SE) — shared trial creds, onboarding checklist (FF-20260122-0987).
- 2026-02-01: Hosted trial start — instrumented token-level telemetry, basic routing rules.
- 2026-02-14: Hosted trial end — handoff notes + initial analysis (see drive doc).
- 2026-02-24: Dedicated demo — runtime capabilities, canary/fallback patterns.
- 2026-03-02: Capacity deep-dive with infra team (Carlos) — provided model latency profiles and concurrency map.
- 2026-03-04: Pricing cadence meeting; finance requested committed QPS/slot numbers for month-to-month and annual options.

Open technical questions (short):
- Exact VPC egress path and NAT throughput required? Need to confirm with their infra.
- KMS integration timeline: can they use existing cloud KMS or require HSM?
- Can we produce a 1-week Dedicated pilot with their traffic shape (bursty QPS) at a reduced rate?

Commercial/forecast notes:
- They are evaluating two purchase models: monthly reserved capacity vs annual commit (preferred if pricing reduces unit cost >25%).
- Finance asked to see ARR scenarios at 50M, 150M, 300M tokens/mo; requested Redwood to convert to monthly $ spend for both hosted vs dedicated.
- Estimated ARR range (customer-provided): $75k–$250k depending on discounting and telemetry add-ons.

Next steps (actionable):
- Redwood: produce Dedicated capacity proposal v1 (slot sizing for sustained 8 QPS, burst headroom to 40 QPS; concurrency config for 80 steady / 200 peak), include recommended GPU counts and quantization profiles. (owner: Carlos)
- Redwood Finance: draft two commercial options (12mo commit & month-to-month) with unit economics and break-even point vs hosted. (owner: Maya)
- Customer: confirm VPC CIDR, egress NAT throughput, and timeline for completing security questionnaire Q3-Q7.
- Schedule procurement sync: proposed 2026-03-10 (hold tentative).

Stitch notes/links: FF call recordings, drive deck (pricing + capacity workbook), active Gmail thread for procurement. Short term blocker: procurement headcount approval + VPC peering window.

CRM shorthand log (recent):
- 2026-03-04 Maya: pricing review call — asked for committed slot numbers; finance wants ARR table.
- 2026-02-24 Carlos: demo — walked through autoscaling + fallback.
- 2026-02-14 SE report: trial telemetry attached to drive (BRK-capacity-forecast-2026.xlsx).

Notes end.
